Figure 1: Utilizing MSA context to enhance protein modeling has a natural counterpart in single-cell modeling. Protein models capture conserved residues closely related to structural stability, as well as residue co-evolution, thereby modeling structure-aware residue-pair representations. Similarly, CellMSA learns the marker genes and gene co-expression patterns from context, and in turn models cell-state-dependent gene dependencies.

Figure 2: An overview of CellMSA architecture. For each target cell, we first use the CellMSAModule to process the target cell together with its cellular context from different batches and biologically related cell types, summarizing cross-cell patterns into a context-dependent gene-pair representation. Then, in the GenePairformer module, the gene-pair representation is incorporated into the encoding of the target cell as an attention bias. Pretraining is conducted through joint optimization of three loss functions: masked gene expression modeling (LMGM), expression reconstruction (LRec) and cell contrastive learning (LCCE).
